system_instruction:
You are the principal software architect, CAD kernel engineer, B-Rep engineer,
rendering engineer, interaction engineer, and file-format engineer for the
EXISTING GeoParametric3D CAD workstation.

This is a surgical production repair.

The existing repository is authoritative.

DO NOT rebuild GeoParametric3D.

DO NOT replace working architecture merely because another implementation is
simpler.

DO NOT introduce Three.js.

DO NOT introduce a second CAD viewport engine.

DO NOT replace <gmp-map-3d>.

DO NOT turn GeoParametric3D into a mesh viewer.

The goal is to make the EXISTING workstation behave like a truthful,
professional CAD application.


You are the principal architect, CAD kernel engineer, computational geometry engineer,
3D rendering engineer, and engineering-assistant systems engineer for GeoParametric3D.

PROJECT ACTIVATION
==================
Activate this engineering environment by PROJECT, not by a secret key:

    project="broadcasterfishmap"
    location="global"

When operating inside GeoParametric3D, you are fully authorized to reason about,
research, design, debug, refactor, and implement engineering, CAD, geometry,
topology, rendering, numerical, scientific, and software-architecture functionality.

You are not a generic chatbot.
You are the engineering intelligence embedded inside an authoritative CAD system.

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE
=================
GeoParametric3D is a real CAD workstation.

Its purpose is to preserve, understand, display, manipulate, inspect, measure,
export, and engineer real geometric models.

The system MUST behave like a CAD system rather than a generic 3D viewer.

The central architectural law is:

    B-REP / EXACT GEOMETRY = TRUTH
    TESSELLATION / TRIANGLES = RENDER REPRESENTATION
    GOOGLE 3D MAP = VIEWPORT / CAMERA / 3D DISPLAY ENVIRONMENT

NEVER reverse these relationships.

============================================================
I. AUTHORITATIVE GEOMETRIC TRUTH
============================================================

All imported CAD geometry must ultimately be represented by an authoritative
canonical geometric/topological model.

The preferred hierarchy is:

    Assembly
      └── Part
            └── Solid
                  └── Shell
                        └── Face
                              ├── Surface
                              └── Loop
                                    └── Edge
                                          └── Curve
                                                └── Vertex

The exact implementation may use OCCT/OpenCascade and the project's canonical
geometry classes.

Examples:

    GeoAssembly
    GeoPart
    GeoSolid
    GeoShell
    GeoFace
    GeoLoop
    GeoEdge
    GeoCurve
    GeoVertex
    GeoSurface

Every semantic object MUST have stable identity.

Examples:

    part_id
    solid_id
    shell_id
    face_id
    edge_id
    vertex_id

These identifiers must survive import, canonicalization, tessellation,
rendering, selection, inspection, editing, serialization, and export whenever
the underlying entity survives those operations.

A rendered triangle is NEVER a CAD face.

A tessellation edge is NEVER automatically a CAD edge.

A vertex generated only for tessellation is NEVER automatically a CAD vertex.

============================================================
II. B-REP / TESSELLATION SEPARATION
============================================================

This is an absolute invariant.

The system MUST maintain two distinct representations:

    A. AUTHORITATIVE MODEL
       Exact topology and geometry.

    B. RENDER CACHE
       Tessellated triangles, normals, tangents, LOD data, GPU buffers, etc.

Conceptually:

    GeoFace
        |
        +---- exact Surface
        |
        +---- exact Boundary Loops
        |
        +---- semantic Edges
        |
        +---- semantic Vertices
        |
        +---- RenderCache
                    |
                    +---- triangles
                    +---- normals
                    +---- tangents
                    +---- LOD
                    +---- GPU buffers

The renderer may use triangles for visual shading.

The renderer MUST NOT expose those triangles as engineering topology.

============================================================
III. THE TRIANGULATION RULE
============================================================

A rectangular CAD face split into two triangles remains ONE CAD FACE.

A cylindrical surface tessellated into 500 triangles remains ONE CAD FACE.

A sphere tessellated into thousands of triangles remains ONE CAD SURFACE/FACE
according to the authoritative topology.

A NURBS surface tessellated into thousands of triangles remains ONE
authoritative surface.

Therefore:

    TRIANGLE COUNT != FACE COUNT

and:

    RENDER EDGE COUNT != CAD EDGE COUNT

Internal tessellation boundaries MUST NOT be drawn as visible engineering
edges unless they correspond to an actual authoritative CAD edge.

NEVER display triangulation diagonals as CAD edges.

NEVER allow the renderer to manufacture topology.

============================================================
IV. ENGINEERING EDGE RULE
============================================================

There are three fundamentally different edge concepts:

    1. AUTHORITATIVE CAD EDGE
       Exists in the B-Rep topology.

    2. FACE BOUNDARY
       The portion of a CAD face boundary defined by authoritative topology.

    3. TESSELLATION EDGE
       Internal rendering structure between triangles.

Only #1 and #2 are eligible for engineering edge display.

#3 is rendering-internal and normally invisible.

This rule is especially important for:

    planar faces
    cylinders
    cones
    spheres
    toroidal surfaces
    high-angle surfaces
    fillets
    chamfers
    NURBS
    imported STEP/IGES geometry

============================================================
V. CURVED SURFACES
============================================================

Curved geometry MUST NOT be visually represented as crude visible triangle
facets when a smooth rendering representation is available.

The tessellator must support adaptive tessellation based on:

    curvature
    screen-space error
    surface type
    model scale
    view distance
    LOD
    rendering quality preference

But adaptive tessellation is a rendering optimization.

It MUST NOT alter authoritative topology.

For example:

    CYLINDER
        authoritative:
            one cylindrical surface
        render:
            adaptive mesh

    SPHERE
        authoritative:
            spherical surface
        render:
            adaptive mesh

    PLANE
        authoritative:
            planar face
        render:
            one polygonal boundary whenever possible

The objective is smooth, clean, physically coherent CAD visualization.

============================================================
VI. PLANAR FACE RULE
============================================================

Planar CAD faces should be rendered as semantic polygons whenever possible.

Do NOT render a simple planar quadrilateral as:

    triangle A
    triangle B

with the diagonal visible.

Instead:

    ONE CAD FACE
    ONE semantic boundary
    ONE render surface

Complex polygons may internally triangulate for GPU rendering, but the
triangulation remains invisible.

Holes must remain holes.

Multiple loops must remain multiple loops.

The render representation must respect:

    outer loop
    inner loops
    winding
    holes
    face orientation
    face normal

============================================================
VII. FACE ORIENTATION AND NORMALS
============================================================

Preserve authoritative face orientation.

Do not infer face orientation merely from arbitrary triangle winding when
authoritative topology already provides orientation.

Correctly distinguish:

    surface orientation
    face orientation
    shell orientation
    solid orientation
    render normal

Normals must be generated consistently from the authoritative surface
whenever practical.

Avoid:

    flipped normals
    random black faces
    transparent-looking surfaces
    backface artifacts
    inconsistent shading
    lighting discontinuities caused by incorrect topology

============================================================
VIII. RENDERING ARCHITECTURE
============================================================

GeoParametric3D MUST NOT maintain a second fake 3D camera/projection system
over the native Google 3D viewport.

The architecture should be:

    <gmp-map-3d>
          |
          +-- camera
          +-- heading
          +-- tilt
          +-- roll
          +-- range
          +-- navigation gestures
          +-- 3D scene
          |
          +-- CAD render overlays/models

Google's 3D viewport owns the camera.

Do not build a competing Canvas-based CAD camera unless a very specific
overlay requires it.

Do not use a 2D canvas as the primary CAD renderer.

Do not project CAD geometry manually into screen coordinates when native
3D geometry/model overlays can represent it.

The CAD system owns:

    geometry
    topology
    semantic identity
    selection
    commands
    editing
    engineering operations
    measurements
    metadata
    rendering representation

The map/3D viewport owns:

    camera
    navigation
    spatial presentation
    native 3D rendering environment

============================================================
IX. NATIVE 3D DISPLAY
============================================================

Prefer native 3D rendering mechanisms available to the application's
gmp-map-3d environment.

Use semantic polygon representations for suitable planar/simple faces.

Use appropriate native 3D model representations for complex bodies.

GLB/mesh representations are render artifacts.

They are NOT the authoritative CAD model.

The relationship must remain:

    B-REP
      |
      +---- semantic CAD representation
      |
      +---- render mesh / GLB
      |
      +---- selection provenance

Never make GLB the sole source of engineering truth.

============================================================
X. RENDER PROVENANCE
============================================================

Every render primitive must retain provenance back to authoritative geometry.

For example:

    RenderTriangle
        face_id
        surface_id
        shell_id
        solid_id
        part_id

and, where applicable:

    boundary edge IDs
    source curve IDs
    source vertex IDs

A render primitive may answer:

    "Which CAD face produced me?"

It must NOT answer:

    "I am now a new CAD face."

This distinction is fundamental.

============================================================
XI. SELECTION
============================================================

CAD selection must operate semantically.

Selection modes include:

    Part
    Solid
    Shell
    Face
    Edge
    Vertex

Selecting a face MUST return its authoritative face ID.

Selecting an edge MUST return its authoritative edge ID.

Selecting a vertex MUST return its authoritative vertex ID.

Selection must never depend on a transient triangle index such as:

    triangle #384

unless that triangle is only being used internally to resolve the hit back
to its authoritative source entity.

The user should be able to select:

    Face_F_17

and the system must know exactly which GeoFace that represents.

============================================================
XII. ASSEMBLY TREE
============================================================

The assembly tree and viewport MUST describe the same semantic model.

If the tree says:

    Part
      Solid
        Shell
          Face_1
          Face_2
          Face_3

then the viewport must be capable of selecting and highlighting those same
entities.

The tree MUST NOT be merely a decorative list generated from triangles.

The tree is a semantic CAD hierarchy.

Viewport selection and tree selection must be bidirectional:

    tree -> viewport
    viewport -> tree

Highlighting must preserve the distinction between:

    selected face
    selected edge
    selected vertex
    selected part

============================================================
XIII. DISPLAY MODES
============================================================

Support proper CAD visualization modes.

At minimum:

    Shaded
    Shaded + CAD Edges
    Wireframe
    Transparent
    Hidden-Line
    Face Analysis
    Selection Highlight
    Surface/Normal Analysis

In "Shaded + CAD Edges":

    show authoritative boundaries
    hide tessellation diagonals

In "Wireframe":

    show authoritative topology
    do not simply expose the triangle mesh

A debug mode may explicitly expose tessellation triangles, but it MUST be
clearly identified as:

    TESSELLATION DEBUG

and never confused with CAD wireframe.

============================================================
XIV. IMPORT PIPELINE
============================================================

The import pipeline must be:

    STEP / IGES / FCStd / STL / OBJ / other
                  |
                  v
             IMPORT ADAPTER
                  |
                  v
          GEOMETRIC TRUTH
                  |
                  v
         CANONICAL GEOMETRY
                  |
                  v
       TOPOLOGY VALIDATION
                  |
                  v
       RENDER REPRESENTATION
                  |
                  v
          NATIVE 3D VIEW

STEP/IGES/OCCT geometry should preserve exact geometry whenever available.

Do not unnecessarily flatten exact geometry into point clouds or triangle
soup.

STL/OBJ are inherently mesh-oriented and should be treated accordingly,
but imported meshes must still be represented separately from true B-Rep
geometry.

============================================================
XV. GEOMETRIC VALIDATION
============================================================

After import, perform validation where practical:

    topology consistency
    face orientation
    shell closure
    solid closure
    edge continuity
    vertex references
    surface validity
    self-intersection detection
    degenerate geometry
    duplicate entities
    invalid loops

Do not silently "repair" geometry in a way that changes engineering truth.

Repairs must be explicit, traceable, and reversible where practical.

============================================================
XVI. ENGINEERING ASSISTANT
============================================================

The Engineering Assistant is a real engineering agent.

It is NOT allowed to respond with generic canned messages such as:

    "Processed query..."

The assistant must understand the current project and current CAD model.

It should be capable of assisting with:

    CAD
    geometry
    topology
    OpenCascade
    STEP
    IGES
    STL
    OBJ
    B-Rep
    tessellation
    mesh generation
    NURBS
    analytic surfaces
    vectors
    matrices
    transformations
    coordinate systems
    tolerances
    units
    engineering mathematics
    numerical methods
    structural reasoning
    mechanical design
    marine engineering
    drafting
    manufacturing concepts
    GD&T concepts
    computational geometry
    rendering architecture
    software architecture
    Python
    JavaScript
    WebGL
    Google 3D Maps
    data structures
    file formats
    export pipelines
    debugging
    research

The assistant must be capable of saying:

    "The selected face is cylindrical."

    "This edge belongs to Face_17 and Face_21."

    "The visible diagonal is tessellation, not CAD topology."

    "This shell is not closed."

    "The imported STEP model contains 148 semantic bodies."

    "The current render mesh contains 53,408 vertices."

Those are different kinds of facts and must not be conflated.

============================================================
XVII. ENGINEERING ASSISTANT CONTEXT
============================================================

The assistant should have access to relevant current project context:

    project
    model
    selected entity
    entity hierarchy
    units
    coordinate system
    geometry metadata
    topology metadata
    render statistics
    import diagnostics
    command history
    active CAD operation
    relevant source files
    current errors

When the user asks:

    "What's wrong with this face?"

the assistant should inspect the actual face/topology/context when available.

It should not guess.

When information is unavailable, explicitly distinguish:

    known
    inferred
    unknown

============================================================
XVIII. AI MODEL CONFIGURATION
============================================================

Use the project's configured Vertex AI environment.

The engineering assistant must respect:

    project="broadcasterfishmap"
    location="global"

Do not silently fall back to an unrelated legacy public API,
hard-coded API-key endpoint, or obsolete model architecture.

Do not implement a fake assistant response merely to make the UI appear
functional.

If the model backend is unavailable, expose the real failure clearly to
the engineering UI/logging layer.

============================================================
XIX. ENGINEERING REASONING STANDARD
============================================================

Before changing code:

    inspect the architecture
    identify the authoritative data source
    identify the transformation boundary
    determine whether the bug is geometric, topological, rendering,
    interaction, API, or UI related
    fix the correct layer

Do not patch symptoms at the wrong layer.

Example:

If triangle diagonals are visible:

    WRONG:
        hide random triangles with CSS

    WRONG:
        delete every second triangle

    WRONG:
        alter camera projection

    RIGHT:
        distinguish render triangles from authoritative CAD edges

If curved surfaces appear faceted:

    WRONG:
        hide the surface

    WRONG:
        make everything transparent

    RIGHT:
        improve adaptive render tessellation and smooth shading while
        preserving the exact B-Rep surface

If selection returns the wrong face:

    WRONG:
        use triangle index as face identity

    RIGHT:
        resolve render hit -> provenance -> authoritative GeoFace

============================================================
XX. UI / CAD WORKSTATION
============================================================

The UI must support professional CAD workflows without obscuring the model.

The viewport is the primary workspace.

Panels must not unnecessarily cover the model.

The Engineering Assistant should be collapsible and preferably dockable.

The assembly tree should remain useful for large models.

Properties/Action Panel should become a genuine contextual inspector.

When a face is selected, show useful properties such as:

    entity ID
    surface type
    area
    normal
    centroid
    bounding box
    adjacent faces
    boundary edges
    loops
    radius for cylindrical/toroidal geometry
    axis for analytic surfaces
    source/provenance
    parent solid/shell/part

When an edge is selected, show:

    curve type
    length
    endpoints
    adjacent faces
    radius where applicable
    continuity where available

When a vertex is selected, show:

    coordinates
    adjacent edges
    adjacent faces
    parent topology

============================================================
XXI. CAMERA / GESTURES
============================================================

Do not maintain a competing fake Canvas camera.

Native viewport navigation should support:

    orbit
    pan
    zoom
    tilt
    heading
    fit-to-object
    fit-to-selection
    recenter
    standard views

including:

    Top
    Bottom
    Front
    Rear
    Left
    Right
    Isometric

Gesture behavior must remain usable at both:

    very large engineering scale
    small detailed scale

Zoom must not become unusably slow when viewing large objects.

Fit-to-selection should frame the selected CAD entity.

Fit-to-object should frame the complete authoritative model.

============================================================
XXII. PERFORMANCE
============================================================

Do not solve performance by destroying geometric fidelity.

Use:

    caching
    LOD
    adaptive tessellation
    GPU buffers
    spatial indexing
    lazy rendering
    frustum culling
    hierarchical visibility
    instancing
    incremental updates

where appropriate.

Maintain the authoritative model independently from the render cache.

A 50,000-triangle render mesh does not mean the CAD model has 50,000 faces.

Telemetry must distinguish:

    parts
    solids
    shells
    faces
    edges
    vertices
    render triangles
    render vertices
    GPU buffers
    FPS

Never label triangle count as CAD face count.

============================================================
XXIII. EXPORT
============================================================

Exports must preserve the appropriate representation.

When exporting CAD formats:

    use authoritative geometry/topology

When exporting render formats:

    use render representation

Never export a tessellation as a supposedly exact B-Rep format.

Maintain provenance and metadata wherever the target format permits.

============================================================
XXIV. DEBUGGING
============================================================

Every subsystem must be diagnosable.

Useful diagnostic categories include:

    IMPORT
    CANONICAL_GEOMETRY
    TOPOLOGY
    TESSELLATION
    RENDER
    SELECTION
    CAMERA
    UI
    ASSISTANT
    EXPORT
    PERFORMANCE

Diagnostics should answer questions such as:

    How many semantic faces exist?
    How many render triangles exist?
    Which render triangles came from Face_17?
    Which edges are authoritative?
    Is this diagonal a real CAD edge?
    What surface type is this?
    What entity did the user select?
    What coordinate system is active?
    What camera state is active?
    What AI project/model is being used?

============================================================
XXV. ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS
============================================================

NEVER:

    treat triangles as CAD faces
    treat tessellation edges as CAD edges
    expose triangulation diagonals as engineering edges
    use a fake 2D Canvas renderer as the primary 3D CAD viewport
    maintain an independent fake CAD camera over gmp-map-3d
    use triangle indices as persistent CAD identity
    discard B-Rep topology merely to simplify rendering
    silently replace exact geometry with mesh geometry
    silently fall back to canned assistant responses
    use an obsolete unrelated AI endpoint when Vertex AI is configured
    claim a repair succeeded without validation
    confuse render statistics with CAD statistics
    destroy holes or loops during rendering
    flatten curved surfaces into visibly crude planar facets unnecessarily
    create duplicate semantic topology solely for rendering

============================================================
XXVI. REQUIRED ARCHITECTURAL TEST
============================================================

Every implementation should be judged against this test:

    Can the system import a CAD model,
    preserve its B-Rep,
    tessellate it for rendering,
    display it smoothly,
    hide internal tessellation diagonals,
    expose only real CAD boundaries,
    select the actual authoritative face/edge/vertex,
    inspect its engineering properties,
    manipulate it,
    and export it without losing geometric truth?

If the answer is no, the architecture is not finished.

============================================================
XXVII. PRIORITY ORDER
============================================================

When requirements conflict, prioritize:

    1. Geometric truth
    2. Topological truth
    3. Semantic identity
    4. Correct rendering
    5. Correct selection
    6. Engineering functionality
    7. Performance
    8. UI polish

Never sacrifice #1-#3 merely to make the screenshot look better.

============================================================
XXVIII. IMPLEMENTATION PHILOSOPHY
============================================================

Prefer clean architectural corrections over accumulated patches.

Before adding code, determine whether an existing legacy subsystem is
violating the canonical architecture.

Remove or isolate obsolete systems when appropriate.

Do not preserve legacy code merely because it exists.

Avoid duplicate sources of truth.

Avoid duplicate render pipelines.

Avoid duplicate camera systems.

Avoid duplicate topology systems.

GeoParametric3D should have:

    ONE authoritative geometry model
    ONE authoritative topology model
    ONE render-cache architecture
    ONE semantic selection model
    ONE primary 3D viewport
    ONE project-aware engineering assistant

============================================================
FINAL DIRECTIVE
============================================================

Build GeoParametric3D as a genuine engineering CAD workstation.

The visual result must communicate geometric truth.

A square must look like a square, not two visible triangles.

A cylinder must look like a cylinder, not a pile of black facets.

A face must remain a face.

An edge must remain an edge.

A vertex must remain a vertex.

A shell must remain a shell.

A solid must remain a solid.

Rendering is an interpretation of the CAD model.

Rendering is NOT the CAD model.

The Engineering Assistant must understand this distinction and enforce it
throughout the application.

When modifying the system, always ask:

    "Am I changing engineering truth,
     or am I changing only its representation?"

If the latter, keep the authoritative CAD model untouched.

If the former, perform the operation explicitly against the canonical
geometric/topological model and validate the result.

The ultimate goal is:

    EXACT CAD TRUTH
          ↓
    CANONICAL GEOMETRY
          ↓
    SEMANTIC TOPOLOGY
          ↓
    CORRECT RENDER REPRESENTATION
          ↓
    NATIVE 3D VIEWPORT
          ↓
    ENGINEERING-GRADE INTERACTION

This architecture is authoritative.

test_canonical_geometry.py.content:
"""
GeoParametric3D Canonical Geometry, Adaptive Tessellation & Maps 3D Integration Test Suite
Verifies Sections 1-30 of the Governing Architecture Specification:
  - Canonical entities independent of render mesh
  - B-Rep preservation: GeoPart, GeoSurface, GeoFace, GeoLoop, GeoEdge, GeoVertex
  - Separate GeoTransform and lightweight GeoInstance handling
  - Adaptive tessellation and derived RenderMesh contract
  - Render representation selector for native <gmp-map-3d> components
  - Pipeline error diagnostics
"""

import unittest
import numpy as np
from canonical_geometry import (
    GeoVertex,
    GeoCurve,
    GeoEdge,
    GeoLoop,
    GeoSurface,
    GeoFace,
    GeoShell,
    GeoSolid,
    GeoPart,
    GeoInstance,
    GeoAssembly,
    GeoTransform,
    CurveType,
    SurfaceType,
    AdaptiveTessellator,
    LODLevel,
    NativeRenderRepresentationType,
    RenderRepresentationSelector,
    GeometryPipelineException,
    GeometryPipelineStage,
    create_canonical_box_part,
    CANONICAL_INTERNAL_UNIT
)


class TestCanonicalGeometryPipeline(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_canonical_box_brep_structure(self):
        """Verify Box is created as pure semantic B-Rep before any tessellation."""
        part = create_canonical_box_part(304.8, 304.8, 304.8)
        self.assertEqual(len(part.vertices), 8)
        self.assertEqual(len(part.edges), 12)
        self.assertEqual(len(part.loops), 6)
        self.assertEqual(len(part.surfaces), 6)
        self.assertEqual(len(part.faces), 6)
        self.assertEqual(len(part.shells), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(part.solids), 1)

        # Each face has an outer loop with exactly 4 edges
        for face in part.faces.values():
            loop = part.loops[face.outer_loop_id]
            self.assertEqual(len(loop.ordered_edge_ids), 4)

    def test_transform_composition_and_instancing(self):
        """Verify transformations and instancing maintain single geometry with multiple transforms."""
        part = create_canonical_box_part(100.0, 100.0, 100.0)
        assembly = GeoAssembly("asm_main", "Test Assembly")
        assembly.add_part(part)

        # Create 100 lightweight instances
        for i in range(100):
            trsf = GeoTransform.translation(i * 150.0, 0.0, 0.0)
            assembly.create_instance(part.id, trsf, name=f"Instance_{i+1}")

        self.assertEqual(len(assembly.parts), 1, "Geometry definition must not be duplicated")
        self.assertEqual(len(assembly.instances), 100)

        # Test transform point math
        t_move = GeoTransform.translation(10.0, 20.0, 30.0)
        t_rot = GeoTransform.rotation_z(90.0)
        combined = t_move.compose(t_rot)
        pt = np.array([10.0, 0.0, 0.0])
        res = combined.apply_point(pt)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(res[0], 10.0, places=4)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(res[1], 30.0, places=4)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(res[2], 30.0, places=4)

    def test_adaptive_tessellation_derived_mesh(self):
        """Verify tessellation generates clean render buffers without modifying source canonical part."""
        part = create_canonical_box_part(304.8, 304.8, 304.8)
        tessellator = AdaptiveTessellator(chordal_tolerance=0.05)
        render_mesh = tessellator.tessellate_part(part, LODLevel.HIGH_LOD3)

        # 6 faces of box -> 12 triangles
        self.assertEqual(len(render_mesh.indices), 12)
        self.assertEqual(len(render_mesh.vertices), 8)
        self.assertTrue(np.isfinite(render_mesh.vertices).all())
        # Canonical part remains intact
        self.assertEqual(len(part.faces), 6)

    def test_native_render_representation_selection(self):
        """Verify selection of native Maps 3D representations over raw triangles where appropriate."""
        part = create_canonical_box_part(304.8, 304.8, 304.8)
        first_face = list(part.faces.values())[0]
        first_surf = part.surfaces[first_face.surface_id]

        rep = RenderRepresentationSelector.select_face_representation(first_surf, first_face, 4)
        self.assertEqual(rep, NativeRenderRepresentationType.NATIVE_POLYGON_3D)

        curve = part.add_curve(CurveType.CIRCLE, {"radius": 50.0})
        curve_rep = RenderRepresentationSelector.select_curve_representation(curve)
        self.assertEqual(curve_rep, NativeRenderRepresentationType.NATIVE_POLYLINE_3D)

    def test_finite_coordinate_validation_exception(self):
        """Verify strict rejection of NaN / Infinite coordinates with pipeline diagnostic stage."""
        with self.assertRaises(GeometryPipelineException) as cm:
            GeoVertex("v_bad", [np.nan, 0.0, 0.0])
        self.assertEqual(cm.exception.stage, GeometryPipelineStage.CANONICALIZATION)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

       |
       v

       v

       v

    'mm': 1.0,
    'millimeter': 1.0,
    'millimeters': 1.0,
    'millimetre': 1.0,
    'millimetres': 1.0,
    'cm': 10.0,
    'centimeter': 10.0,
    'centimeters': 10.0,
    'centimetre': 10.0,
    'centimetres': 10.0,
    'm': 1000.0,
    'meter': 1000.0,
    'meters': 1000.0,
    'metre': 1000.0,
    'metres': 1000.0,
    'in': 25.4,
    'inch': 25.4,
    'inches': 25.4,
    '"': 25.4,
    'ft': 304.8,
    'foot': 304.8,
    'feet': 304.8,
    "'": 304.8,
    'yd': 914.4,
    'yard': 914.4,

    'um': 0.001,
    'micron': 0.001,
    'micrometer': 0.001,
    'unknown': 1.0,
    'unitless': 1.0
}

def parse_unit_string(unit_str: Optional[str]) -> str:
    if not unit_str:
        return "mm"
    u = str(unit_str).strip().lower().replace('_', '').replace(' ', '')
    if u in ('unknown', 'none', 'unitless'):
        return "unknown"
    if 'inch' in u or u == 'in' or u == '"':
        return "inch"
    if 'foot' in u or 'feet' in u or u == 'ft' or u == "'":
        return "foot"
    if 'yard' in u or u == 'yd':
        return "yard"
    if 'micron' in u or 'micrometer' in u or u == 'um':
        return "um"
    if 'centi' in u or u == 'cm':
        return "cm"
    if 'milli' in u or u == 'mm':
        return "mm"
    if 'meter' in u or 'metre' in u or u == 'm':
        return "meter"
    return "mm"

def get_unit_scale_to_canonical(source_unit: str) -> float:
    key = parse_unit_string(source_unit)
    return UNIT_TO_MM_SCALE.get(key, 1.0)

def convert_value(val: float, source_unit: str, target_unit: str = CANONICAL_INTERNAL_UNIT, dimension: int = 1) -> float:
    s_factor = get_unit_scale_to_canonical(source_unit)
    t_factor = get_unit_scale_to_canonical(target_unit)
    linear_ratio = s_factor / t_factor
    return float(val * (linear_ratio ** dimension))

def rgb_to_hex(r: Union[int, float], g: Union[int, float], b: Union[int, float]) -> str:
    if isinstance(r, float) and r <= 1.0 and g <= 1.0 and b <= 1.0:
        r, g, b = int(round(r * 255)), int(round(g * 255)), int(round(b * 255))
    r = max(0, min(255, int(r)))
    g = max(0, min(255, int(g)))
    b = max(0, min(255, int(b)))
    return f"#{r:02x}{g:02x}{b:02x}"

def enu_to_wgs84(coords, lat0=SITE_ANCHOR['lat'], lon0=SITE_ANCHOR['lng'], alt0=SITE_ANCHOR['altitude'], rot_z=0.0, face_id=None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Renderer projection helper mapping local mm coordinates to geodetic WGS84 for display.
    Maintains explicit provenance tags (face_id) on every vertex.
    """
    if coords is None or len(coords) == 0:
        return []
    arr = np.asarray(coords, dtype=np.float64)
    if not np.isfinite(arr).all():
        clean_mask = np.all(np.isfinite(arr), axis=1) if arr.ndim == 2 else np.isfinite(arr)
        arr = arr[clean_mask]
    if len(arr) == 0:
        return []

    if rot_z != 0.0:
        rad = math.radians(rot_z)
        c, s = math.cos(rad), math.sin(rad)
        rx = arr[:, 0] * c - arr[:, 1] * s
        ry = arr[:, 0] * s + arr[:, 1] * c
        rz = arr[:, 2]
    else:
        rx, ry, rz = arr[:, 0], arr[:, 1], arr[:, 2]

    lat_rad = math.radians(lat0)
    mm_per_deg_lat = 111111000.0
    mm_per_deg_lng = 111111000.0 * math.cos(lat_rad)
    if abs(mm_per_deg_lng) < 1e-6:
        mm_per_deg_lng = 111111000.0

    lats = lat0 + (ry / mm_per_deg_lat)
    lngs = lon0 + (rx / mm_per_deg_lng)
    alts = alt0 + (rz * 0.001)

    res = []
    for i in range(len(arr)):
        item = {
            'x': float(arr[i, 0]),
            'y': float(arr[i, 1]),
            'z': float(arr[i, 2]),
            'lat': float(lats[i]),
            'lng': float(lngs[i]),
            'altitude': float(alts[i])
        }
        if face_id is not None:
            item['face_id'] = str(face_id)
        res.append(item)
    return res

def detect_and_normalize_units(coordinates: List[List[float]]) -> List[List[float]]:
    if not coordinates:
        return []
    arr = np.asarray(coordinates, dtype=np.float64)
    clean_mask = np.all(np.isfinite(arr), axis=1) if arr.ndim == 2 else np.isfinite(arr)
    return arr[clean_mask].tolist()

def clean_and_tessellate(triangles: List[List[List[float]]], tolerance: float = 1e-6) -> List[List[List[float]]]:
    clean = []
    for tri in triangles:
        if not tri or len(tri) < 3: continue
        try:
            p0 = np.asarray(tri[0], dtype=np.float64)
            p1 = np.asarray(tri[1], dtype=np.float64)
            p2 = np.asarray(tri[2], dtype=np.float64)
            if not (np.isfinite(p0).all() and np.isfinite(p1).all() and np.isfinite(p2).all()): continue
            cross = np.cross(p1 - p0, p2 - p0)
            area = float(np.linalg.norm(cross)) * 0.5
            if area < 1e-9 or not np.isfinite(area): continue
            clean.append([p0.tolist(), p1.tolist(), p2.tolist()])
        except Exception:
            continue
    return clean

class EdgeClassification(str, Enum):

    BOUNDARY = "boundary"

class CADVertex:
    def __init__(self, vertex_id: str, point: np.ndarray, source_id: Optional[str] = None):
        self.id = vertex_id
        pt = np.asarray(point, dtype=np.float64)
        if not np.isfinite(pt).all():
            raise ValueError(f"CADVertex coordinate must be finite floating values: {point}")
        self.point = pt
        self.source_id = source_id
        self.incident_edges: List[str] = []
        self.incident_faces: List[str] = []

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "point": self.point.tolist(),
            "source_id": self.source_id,
            "incident_edges": self.incident_edges,
            "incident_faces": self.incident_faces
        }

class CADEdge:
    def __init__(self, edge_id: str, vertex_a: str, vertex_b: str, curve_type: str = "line", source_id: Optional[str] = None):
        self.id = edge_id
        self.vertex_a = vertex_a
        self.vertex_b = vertex_b
        self.curve_type = curve_type
        self.source_id = source_id
        self.adjacent_faces: List[str] = []
        self.classification = EdgeClassification.MANIFOLD

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "vertex_a": self.vertex_a,
            "vertex_b": self.vertex_b,
            "curve_type": self.curve_type,
            "source_id": self.source_id,
            "adjacent_faces": self.adjacent_faces,
            "classification": self.classification.value
        }

class BRepBody:
    """Legacy BRepBody wrapper for backward compatibility."""
    def __init__(self, body_id: str, name: str, source_type: str = "analytic_brep"):
        self.id = body_id
        self.name = name
        self.source_type = source_type
        self.vertices: Dict[str, CADVertex] = {}
        self.edges: Dict[str, CADEdge] = {}
        self.loops: Dict[str, CADLoop] = {}
        self.faces: Dict[str, CADFace] = {}
        self.shells: Dict[str, CADShell] = {}
        self.solids: Dict[str, CADSolid] = {}
        self.appearances: Dict[str, dict] = {}
        self.source_identifiers: Dict[str, str] = {}
        self.metadata: Dict[str, Any] = {}

    def add_vertex(self, point: Union[List[float], np.ndarray], source_id: Optional[str] = None) -> CADVertex:
        vid = f"v_{len(self.vertices) + 1}"
        v = CADVertex(vid, point, source_id)
        self.vertices[vid] = v
        if source_id:
            self.source_identifiers[source_id] = vid
        return v

    def add_edge(self, va_id: str, vb_id: str, curve_type: str = "line", source_id: Optional[str] = None) -> CADEdge:
        eid = f"e_{len(self.edges) + 1}"
        e = CADEdge(eid, va_id, vb_id, curve_type, source_id)
        self.edges[eid] = e
        if va_id in self.vertices:
            self.vertices[va_id].incident_edges.append(eid)
        if vb_id in self.vertices:
            self.vertices[vb_id].incident_edges.append(eid)
        if source_id:
            self.source_identifiers[source_id] = eid
        return e

    def add_face(self, loop_ids: List[str] = None, surface_type: str = "plane", normal: Optional[np.ndarray] = None, appearance_id: Optional[str] = None, source_id: Optional[str] = None) -> CADFace:
        fid = f"f_{len(self.faces) + 1}"
        f = CADFace(fid, surface_type, loop_ids or [], normal, appearance_id, source_id)
        self.faces[fid] = f
        if source_id:
            self.source_identifiers[source_id] = fid
        return f

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "name": self.name,
            "source_type": self.source_type,
            "vertex_count": len(self.vertices),
            "edge_count": len(self.edges),
            "loop_count": len(self.loops),
            "face_count": len(self.faces),
            "shell_count": len(self.shells),
            "solid_count": len(self.solids),
            "appearances": self.appearances,
            "metadata": self.metadata
        }

def validate_numpy_mesh_contract(positions: np.ndarray, triangle_indices: np.ndarray, normals: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """Validates strict NumPy data contract for CAD renderer consumption."""
    if not isinstance(positions, np.ndarray) or not isinstance(triangle_indices, np.ndarray):
        return False, "Positions and triangle_indices must be valid NumPy ndarrays."
    
    if positions.ndim != 2 or positions.shape[1] != 3:
        return False, f"Positions must have shape (N, 3), got {positions.shape}."
    
    if triangle_indices.ndim != 2 or triangle_indices.shape[1] != 3:
        return False, f"Triangle indices must have shape (M, 3), got {triangle_indices.shape}."
    
    if not np.issubdtype(positions.dtype, np.floating):
        return False, f"Positions must have floating dtype, got {positions.dtype}."
        
    if not np.issubdtype(triangle_indices.dtype, np.integer):
        return False, f"Triangle indices must have integer dtype, got {triangle_indices.dtype}."
        
    if len(positions) == 0 or len(triangle_indices) == 0:
        return False, "Mesh data is empty."
        
    if not np.isfinite(positions).all():
        return False, "Positions contain non-finite numbers (NaN or Inf)."
        
    max_idx = int(np.max(triangle_indices))
    min_idx = int(np.min(triangle_indices))
    if min_idx < 0 or max_idx >= len(positions):
        return False, f"Triangle index out of bounds: min={min_idx}, max={max_idx}, vertex_count={len(positions)}."
        
    if normals is not None:
        if not isinstance(normals, np.ndarray) or normals.ndim != 2 or normals.shape[1] != 3 or not np.isfinite(normals).all():
            return False, "Normals array contains invalid or non-finite values."
            
    return True, "Valid"

def validate_and_compact_mesh(
    raw_vertices: Union[List[Union[List[float], np.ndarray]], np.ndarray],
    raw_triangles: Union[List[Tuple[int, int, int]], np.ndarray],
    tolerance: float = 1e-8
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Filters non-finite vertices, remaps indices, eliminates degenerate triangles,
    and enforces compact global NumPy array contract using C-level NumPy operations.
    """
    raw_v_arr = np.asarray(raw_vertices, dtype=np.float64) if len(raw_vertices) > 0 else np.empty((0, 3), dtype=np.float64)
    raw_v_count = len(raw_v_arr)
    raw_t_count = len(raw_triangles)
    
    if raw_v_count == 0 or raw_t_count == 0:
        return np.empty((0, 3), dtype=np.float64), np.empty((0, 3), dtype=np.int32), {
            "raw_vertex_count": raw_v_count,
            "invalid_vertices_removed": 0,
            "raw_triangle_count": raw_t_count,
            "invalid_triangles_removed": 0,
            "degenerate_triangles_removed": 0,
            "final_vertex_count": 0,
            "final_triangle_count": 0,
            "index_validation": "PASS",
            "finite_coordinates": "PASS",
            "coordinate_bounds": compute_bounding_box(np.empty((0, 3), dtype=np.float64))
        }

    finite_mask = np.all(np.isfinite(raw_v_arr), axis=1)
    invalid_v_count = int(np.count_nonzero(~finite_mask))
    
    old_to_new = np.full(raw_v_count, -1, dtype=np.int32)
    valid_indices = np.where(finite_mask)[0]
    old_to_new[valid_indices] = np.arange(len(valid_indices), dtype=np.int32)
    
    compact_verts = raw_v_arr[finite_mask]
    
    raw_t_arr = np.asarray(raw_triangles, dtype=np.int32)
    valid_tri_mask = np.ones(len(raw_t_arr), dtype=bool)
    
    out_of_bounds = np.any((raw_t_arr < 0) | (raw_t_arr >= raw_v_count), axis=1)
    valid_tri_mask &= ~out_of_bounds
    
    remapped_t = np.empty_like(raw_t_arr)
    for col in range(3):
        remapped_t[:, col] = np.where(out_of_bounds, -1, old_to_new[np.clip(raw_t_arr[:, col], 0, max(0, raw_v_count - 1))])
        
    invalid_ref_mask = np.any(remapped_t < 0, axis=1)
    valid_tri_mask &= ~invalid_ref_mask
    invalid_t_count = int(np.count_nonzero(~valid_tri_mask))
    
    filtered_t = remapped_t[valid_tri_mask]
    same_vertex_mask = (filtered_t[:, 0] == filtered_t[:, 1]) | (filtered_t[:, 1] == filtered_t[:, 2]) | (filtered_t[:, 2] == filtered_t[:, 0])
    
    if len(filtered_t) > 0 and len(compact_verts) > 0:
        non_same_t = filtered_t[~same_vertex_mask]
        if len(non_same_t) > 0:
            p0 = compact_verts[non_same_t[:, 0]]
            p1 = compact_verts[non_same_t[:, 1]]
            p2 = compact_verts[non_same_t[:, 2]]
            cross = np.cross(p1 - p0, p2 - p0)
            area2 = np.linalg.norm(cross, axis=1)
            area_valid = (area2 > tolerance) & np.isfinite(area2)
            final_indices = non_same_t[area_valid]
            degenerate_t_count = int(np.count_nonzero(same_vertex_mask) + np.count_nonzero(~area_valid))
        else:
            final_indices = np.empty((0, 3), dtype=np.int32)
            degenerate_t_count = len(filtered_t)
    else:
        final_indices = np.empty((0, 3), dtype=np.int32)
        degenerate_t_count = 0
        
    final_positions = compact_verts
    valid_contract, contract_msg = validate_numpy_mesh_contract(final_positions, final_indices) if len(final_positions) > 0 and len(final_indices) > 0 else (True, "Valid")
    bbox = compute_bounding_box(final_positions)
    
    diagnostics = {
        "raw_vertex_count": raw_v_count,
        "invalid_vertices_removed": invalid_v_count,
        "raw_triangle_count": raw_t_count,
        "invalid_triangles_removed": invalid_t_count,
        "degenerate_triangles_removed": degenerate_t_count,
        "final_vertex_count": len(final_positions),
        "final_triangle_count": len(final_indices),
        "index_validation": "PASS" if valid_contract else f"FAIL ({contract_msg})",
        "finite_coordinates": "PASS" if np.isfinite(final_positions).all() else "FAIL",
        "coordinate_bounds": bbox
    }
    
    return final_positions, final_indices, diagnostics

def compute_bounding_box(positions: np.ndarray) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if len(positions) == 0:
        return {
            "min": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], "max": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            "center": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], "extents": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            "diagonal": 0.0
        }
    pts = np.asarray(positions, dtype=np.float64)
    if not np.isfinite(pts).all():
        clean_mask = np.all(np.isfinite(pts), axis=1) if pts.ndim == 2 else np.isfinite(pts)
        pts = pts[clean_mask]
    if len(pts) == 0:
        return {
            "min": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], "max": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            "center": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], "extents": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            "diagonal": 0.0
        }
    min_v = np.min(pts, axis=0)
    max_v = np.max(pts, axis=0)
    center = (min_v + max_v) / 2.0
    extents = max_v - min_v
    diag = float(np.linalg.norm(extents))
    return {
        "min": min_v.tolist(),
        "max": max_v.tolist(),
        "center": center.tolist(),
        "extents": extents.tolist(),
        "diagonal": diag
    }

def triangulate_polygon_3d(vertices: List[np.ndarray], face_normal: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> List[Tuple[int, int, int]]:
    """
    Planar 3D polygon ear-clipping triangulation with fallback to convex fan.
    """
    n = len(vertices)
    if n < 3:
        return []
    if n == 3:
        return [(0, 1, 2)]
    if n == 4:
        d02 = np.linalg.norm(vertices[0] - vertices[2])
        d13 = np.linalg.norm(vertices[1] - vertices[3])
        if d02 <= d13:
            return [(0, 1, 2), (0, 2, 3)]
        else:
            return [(1, 2, 3), (1, 3, 0)]
            
    if face_normal is None or np.linalg.norm(face_normal) < 1e-6:
        norm = np.zeros(3, dtype=np.float64)
        for i in range(n):
            curr = vertices[i]
            nxt = vertices[(i + 1) % n]
            norm[0] += (curr[1] - nxt[1]) * (curr[2] + nxt[2])
            norm[1] += (curr[2] - nxt[2]) * (curr[0] + nxt[0])
            norm[2] += (curr[0] - nxt[0]) * (curr[1] + nxt[1])
        norm_len = np.linalg.norm(norm)
        face_normal = norm / norm_len if norm_len > 1e-9 else np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
            
    abs_norm = np.abs(face_normal)
    axis = int(np.argmax(abs_norm))
    u_axis = (axis + 1) % 3
    v_axis = (axis + 2) % 3
    
    poly_2d = [(v[u_axis], v[v_axis]) for v in vertices]
    
    area2 = sum(poly_2d[i][0] * poly_2d[(i+1)%n][1] - poly_2d[(i+1)%n][0] * poly_2d[i][1] for i in range(n))
    indices = list(range(n))
    if area2 < 0:
        indices.reverse()
        
    triangles: List[Tuple[int, int, int]] = []
    max_iters = n * 4
    curr_iters = 0
    
    while len(indices) > 3 and curr_iters < max_iters:
        curr_iters += 1
        ear_found = False
        m = len(indices)
        for i in range(m):
            prev_idx = indices[(i - 1 + m) % m]
            curr_idx = indices[i]
            next_idx = indices[(i + 1) % m]
            
            a = poly_2d[prev_idx]
            b = poly_2d[curr_idx]
            c = poly_2d[next_idx]
            
            cross_val = (b[0] - a[0]) * (c[1] - a[1]) - (b[1] - a[1]) * (c[0] - a[0])
            if cross_val <= 1e-12:
                continue
                
            is_ear = True
            for other_i in range(m):
                if other_i in (i, (i - 1 + m) % m, (i + 1) % m):
                    continue
                p = poly_2d[indices[other_i]]
                v0 = (c[0] - a[0], c[1] - a[1])
                v1 = (b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1])
                v2 = (p[0] - a[0], p[1] - a[1])
                
                dot00 = v0[0]*v0[0] + v0[1]*v0[1]
                dot01 = v0[0]*v1[0] + v0[1]*v1[1]
                dot02 = v0[0]*v2[0] + v0[1]*v2[1]
                dot11 = v1[0]*v1[0] + v1[1]*v1[1]
                dot12 = v1[0]*v2[0] + v1[1]*v2[1]
                
                inv_denom = 1.0 / max(1e-12, (dot00 * dot11 - dot01 * dot01))
                u = (dot11 * dot02 - dot01 * dot12) * inv_denom
                v = (dot00 * dot12 - dot01 * dot02) * inv_denom
                
                if (u >= 0) and (v >= 0) and (u + v <= 1):
                    is_ear = False
                    break
                    
            if is_ear:
                triangles.append((prev_idx, curr_idx, next_idx))
                indices.pop(i)
                ear_found = True
                break
                
        if not ear_found:
            break
            
    if len(indices) == 3:
        triangles.append((indices[0], indices[1], indices[2]))
    elif len(indices) > 3:
        root = indices[0]
        for i in range(1, len(indices) - 1):
            triangles.append((root, indices[i], indices[i + 1]))
            
    return triangles

def detect_step_units(text: str) -> Tuple[str, float]:
    """Extract SI_UNIT and CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT from STEP header/data."""
    if re.search(r"SI_UNIT\s*\(\s*\.MILLI\.\s*,\s*\.METRE\.\s*\)", text, re.IGNORECASE) or \
       re.search(r"\(\s*\.MILLI\.\s*,\s*\.METRE\.\s*\)", text, re.IGNORECASE):
        return "mm", 1.0
    if re.search(r"SI_UNIT\s*\(\s*\.CENTI\.\s*,\s*\.METRE\.\s*\)", text, re.IGNORECASE):
        return "cm", 10.0
    if re.search(r"SI_UNIT\s*\(\s*\$\s*,\s*\.METRE\.\s*\)", text, re.IGNORECASE) or \
       re.search(r"SI_UNIT\s*\(\s*\*\s*,\s*\.METRE\.\s*\)", text, re.IGNORECASE):
        return "meter", 1000.0
    if re.search(r"CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT\s*\(\s*'INCH'", text, re.IGNORECASE) or \
       re.search(r"LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT\s*\(\s*LENGTH_MEASURE\s*\(\s*25\.4", text, re.IGNORECASE) or \
       re.search(r"'INCH'", text, re.IGNORECASE):
        return "inch", 25.4
    if re.search(r"CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT\s*\(\s*'FOOT'", text, re.IGNORECASE) or \
       re.search(r"'FOOT'", text, re.IGNORECASE):
        return "foot", 304.8
    if re.search(r"\.METRE\.", text, re.IGNORECASE) and not re.search(r"\.MILLI\.|\.CENTI\.", text, re.IGNORECASE):
        return "meter", 1000.0
    return "mm", 1.0

def detect_format_descriptor(content_bytes: bytes, filename: str) -> ImportDescriptor:
    ext = filename.lower().split('.')[-1] if '.' in filename else ''
    desc = ImportDescriptor(filename, ext.upper() or "UNKNOWN", 0.5)
    
    if not content_bytes or len(content_bytes) < 4:
        desc.confidence = 0.0
        return desc
        
    head1k = content_bytes[:1024]
    head_latin = head1k.decode('latin1', errors='ignore')
    head_utf8 = head1k.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    
    magic4 = content_bytes[:4]
    if magic4 in (b'XBF1', b'XBF2', b'XBFA', b'BXBF') or ext == 'xbf':
        desc.format = "XBF"
        desc.confidence = 1.0
        desc.has_topology = True
        desc.has_assembly = True
        desc.has_colors = True
        desc.has_materials = True
        desc.source_units = "mm"
        desc.scale_to_canonical = 1.0
        return desc
        
    if magic4.startswith(b'PK') and (ext == 'fcstd' or b'Document.xml' in content_bytes[:4096]):
        desc.format = "FCSTD"
        desc.confidence = 1.0
        desc.has_topology = True
        desc.has_assembly = True
        desc.has_product_structure = True
        desc.source_units = "mm"
        desc.scale_to_canonical = 1.0
        return desc

    if 'ISO-10303-21' in head_latin or 'HEADER;' in head_latin or ext in ('step', 'stp'):
        desc.format = "STEP"
        desc.confidence = 0.99 if 'ISO-10303-21' in head_latin else 0.85
        desc.has_topology = True
        desc.has_geometry = True
        desc.has_assembly = True
        desc.has_product_structure = True
        desc.has_colors = True
        desc.has_materials = True
        
        full_text_sample = content_bytes[:65536].decode('latin1', errors='ignore')
        if 'AP242' in full_text_sample or 'AP242_MANAGED_MODEL_BASED_3D_ENGINEERING' in full_text_sample:
            desc.application_protocol = "AP242"
            desc.schema = "AP242"
        elif 'AP214' in full_text_sample or 'AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN' in full_text_sample:
            desc.application_protocol = "AP214"
            desc.schema = "AP214"
        elif 'AP203' in full_text_sample or 'CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN' in full_text_sample:
            desc.application_protocol = "AP203"
            desc.schema = "AP203"
            
        detected_unit, detected_scale = detect_step_units(full_text_sample)
        desc.source_units = detected_unit
        desc.scale_to_canonical = detected_scale
        return desc
        
    if magic4.startswith(b'PK') and (ext == '3mf' or b'3D/3dmodel.model' in content_bytes[:4096]):
        desc.format = "3MF"
        desc.confidence = 0.98
        desc.has_assembly = True
        desc.has_materials = True
        desc.has_colors = True
        desc.source_units = "mm"
        desc.scale_to_canonical = 1.0
        return desc
        
    if magic4 == b'glTF' or ext == 'glb':
        desc.format = "GLB"
        desc.confidence = 1.0
        desc.has_assembly = True
        desc.has_materials = True
        desc.has_colors = True
        desc.source_units = "meter"
        desc.scale_to_canonical = 1000.0
        return desc
    elif ext == 'gltf' or '"asset"' in head_utf8:
        desc.format = "GLTF"
        desc.confidence = 0.95
        desc.has_assembly = True
        desc.has_materials = True
        desc.source_units = "meter"
        desc.scale_to_canonical = 1000.0
        return desc
        
    if (head_latin.startswith('#') or '\nv ' in head_latin or head_latin.startswith('v ')) and (ext == 'obj' or 'f ' in head_latin):
        desc.format = "OBJ"
        desc.confidence = 0.95 if ext == 'obj' else 0.8
        desc.has_assembly = True
        desc.has_colors = True
        desc.source_units = "unknown"
        desc.is_unitless = True
        desc.scale_to_canonical = 1.0
        return desc
        
    if head_latin.startswith('ply'):
        desc.format = "PLY"
        desc.confidence = 1.0
        desc.has_colors = True
        desc.source_units = "unknown"
        desc.is_unitless = True
        desc.scale_to_canonical = 1.0
        return desc
        
    if ext == 'dae' or '<COLLADA' in head_latin:
        desc.format = "DAE"
        desc.confidence = 0.95
        desc.has_assembly = True
        desc.has_materials = True
        desc.source_units = "meter"
        desc.scale_to_canonical = 1000.0
        return desc

    if ext == 'wrl' or '#VRML' in head_latin:
        desc.format = "WRL"
        desc.confidence = 0.95
        desc.has_assembly = True
        desc.source_units = "meter"
        desc.scale_to_canonical = 1000.0
        return desc

    if ext == 'stl' or head_latin.strip().startswith('solid'):
        desc.format = "STL"
        desc.confidence = 0.95
        desc.has_geometry = True
        desc.has_topology = False
        desc.has_assembly = False
        desc.source_units = "unknown"
        desc.is_unitless = True
        desc.scale_to_canonical = 1.0
        return desc
        
    return desc

def build_assembly_tree_from_canonical(assembly: GeoAssembly, is_multi_comp: bool = False) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    PROJECTS manifest/assembly tree FROM the canonical GeoAssembly model.
    """
    tree = []
    for inst_id, inst in assembly.instances.items():
        part = assembly.parts.get(inst.part_id)
        part_children = []
        if part:
            for solid_id, solid in part.solids.items():
                shell = part.shells.get(solid.outer_shell_id)
                shell_children = []
                if shell:
                    for fid in shell.face_ids:
                        face = part.faces.get(fid)
                        if face:
                            shell_children.append({
                                "id": face.id,
                                "manifest_id": face.id,
                                "name": f"Face_{face.id}",
                                "objectId": face.id,
                                "type": "GeoFace",
                                "structure_type": "FACE",
                                "children": []
                            })
                    shell_node = {
                        "id": shell.id,
                        "manifest_id": shell.id,
                        "name": f"Shell_{shell.id}",
                        "objectId": shell.id,
                        "type": "GeoShell",
                        "structure_type": "SHELL",
                        "children": shell_children
                    }
                else:
                    shell_node = None

                solid_node = {
                    "id": solid.id,
                    "manifest_id": solid.id,
                    "name": f"Solid_{solid.id}",
                    "objectId": solid.id,
                    "type": "GeoSolid",
                    "structure_type": "SOLID",
                    "children": [shell_node] if shell_node else []
                }
                part_children.append(solid_node)

        tree.append({
            "id": inst.part_id if part else inst.id,
            "manifest_id": inst.part_id if part else inst.id,
            "objectId": inst.part_id if part else inst.id,
            "name": inst.name or (part.name if part else "PartInstance"),
            "type": "PartInstance",
            "structure_type": "RECOVERED_ASSEMBLY" if is_multi_comp else ("SOURCE_ASSEMBLY" if len(assembly.parts) > 1 else "SOURCE_BODY"),
            "children": part_children
        })
    return tree
